questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good English skills in the Netherlands. Nice infrastructure to travel to other countries easily. A language I didn't know so I could feel like I was far away (even though I could take a flight back in less than 2 hours)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My student housing was really bad, but overall I really enjoyed both the Dutch and the friends I made. And the university, of course.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. And people are very helpful and effective, so emails are responded to fast.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university provided a Welcome program with all information needed. The orientation was both socially and educationally super good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find it - but the opportunities are super limited. I could more or less only choose SSH, Short Stay Housing, in either Science Park or nearer the city. I chose the latter and I enjoyed not living on campus. Still only 10 minutes to go there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is really nice to be able to catch a train from the Central station fast, to meet friends in the center etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the housing I lived in at Pythagoraslaan extremely unsatisfying. The place was dirty, old and I had mold in my room no one from the company took care of. I was often awake because of noice from parties (it's a student housing complex, so it's nice to live many young people together, but if you, like me, prefer sleeping well 6-8 hours per nice also in the weekends, you should consider something more private and not a student housing party mekka like De Sterren)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The International Office was a great help with all questions.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was easy to contact the International Office and I was able to change courses the day before my arrival without further problems.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Office could answer all questions I had. Also, I had an "Academic Buddy" who helped me with both academic stuff but also to translate things from Dutch-English e.g. in the process to register at the municipality.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very much indeed, it was easy and also to change if necessary. I had to change because my number 1 priority unluckily got fully booked.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose something of interest! And were the exams will be fairly easy to pass. You don't need to think about career possibilities already, you will regret it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would have wished more sociology classes, since I'm a sociology student.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very high. But more like in high school with emphasis on tutorials and mandatory presence. I did not really like that since I'm used to schedule my time on my own and be responsible myself for my learning.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different, as mentioned, as in high school with teachers pointing at us if no one speaks up.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Criminal Behavior during the Lifecourse
Health in Society
Science of Happiness
Youth Culture in a Digital would

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Youth Culture and Criminal Behavior were very interesting.

questions.answer: Paying for bedsheets when I came.

questions.answer: Everything is cheaper than in DK

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sport facilities are awesome at campus

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything basically

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend the gym, making friends in the Orientation Week and of course if you live in a student housing - you will never be alone. Remember to breathe sometimes and go for a walk alone as well.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to Paris, Berlin, Luxemburg, etc.! The opportunities are so good and trains are super fast and accessible.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy indeed, basically the Dutch are like Danes, though we are a bit more relaxed I would say. The Dutch are super productive

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Orientation Week was the bomb!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The local students are not really interested in internationals.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The canals, the big windows, the Christmas traditions!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Vær opmærksom på, at SSH udbyder rimelig hæslige værelser. Jeg boede som sagt i De Sterren og vores toiletter stoppede ofte så meget, at vi havde kloakvand til anklerne (seriøst). Jeg havde også skimmel på mit værelse og kunne høre ALT fra de andres værelser og fra stuen. Så hvis du elsker konstant stimuli og at bo med +10 mennesker, go for it! Jeg var selv bare virkelig blevet for gammel til dét og ville så gerne være alene bare nogle gange (er tidligere højskoleelev og har været på Roskilde seks gange, dette var klart hårdere) og have en "voksen", der kunne hjælpe med alt det, der virkede uoverskueligt, f.eks. skimmelsvampen. Jeg ville ønske jeg havde haft mere rene faciliteter, der var virkelig klamt ofte. Jo flere, du bor med, jo mindre gider de at rydde op efter sig selv. Men men men - jeg er selvfølgelig mega glad for, at jeg fik 10 virkelig gode venner, da det hele var overstået, så det var jo klart fordelen. Jeg ved fra andre, at det kan være ensomt kun at bo med 1-2 andre, fordi man ikke nødvendigvis kommer hjem til nogen hver dag. Og det er især vigtigt i starten, hvor alt er lidt overvældende. Jeg ville have boet i Johanna Building eller privat (dog røvdyrt), hvis jeg kunne lave det om.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Vær opmærksom på, at det faglige niveau er højt, og det forventes, at du aktivt deltager flere gange i hver time. Så man kan altså ikke tage en slapper, selvom man (læs: jeg) ellers havde håbet på dét.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Engelskkundskaber, fantastiske venner, fantastisk by. En masse rejseminder. At jeg gjorde det! Der var mange nedture, men på den anden side har jeg lært SÅ meget om mig selv og om, hvad jeg ønsker for fremtiden. Det har været alle tudeturene værd.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My student housing

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy it, relax, go for it. Remember to take care of yourself.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
